text:
If only the sun would shine tonight

If, in the depths of the Opera, two clear and radiant breasts

Composed for the word love the most marvelous living illuminated initial

If the wooden pavement opened over the summit of the mountains

If the ermine looked with a beseeching gesture

At the red-bandaged priest

Who returns from prison counting the closed cars

If the luxurious echo of the rivers I torment

Would only cast my body onto the grass of Paris

That does not freeze inside the jewelry shops

At least spring would no longer frighten me

If only I were a root of the tree of heaven

At last goodness in the sugarcane of air

What do you see, beautiful silent one

Beneath the Arc de Triomphe of the Carrousel

If pleasure ruled under the aspect of an eternal passerby

While the Chambers were furrowed only by the violet gaze of the promenades

What would I not give for an arm of the Seine to slide beneath the Morning

Which is lost in any case

I do not resign myself, no, to the caressing rooms

Where the telephone of the night's fines rings

On leaving I set fire to a lock of hair

which is the fuse of a bomb

And the lock of hair digs a tunnel beneath Paris

If only my train would enter through that tunnel

translation.title: The Plume
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Breton’s conditional cascade, Parisian locations, and explosive hair-fuse image.
